generated_note: Collected via web research; verify before clinical use.

books.title: The Handbook of Emotional Intelligence: The Theory and Practice of Development, Evaluation, Education, and Application - at Home, School, and in the Workplace
books.author: Reuven Bar-On; James D. A. Parker (Eds.)
books.summary: Comprehensive scholarly handbook (Jossey-Bass/Wiley, foreword by Daniel Goleman) covering the theory, measurement, development, and application of emotional intelligence across home, school, and workplace settings, including conceptual models and assessment methods such as the EQ-i.
books.clinical_usage: Reference text for clinicians who want a rigorous grounding in competing EI models and validated assessment options before integrating EI constructs into case formulation or psychoeducation.

books.title: Emotional Development and Emotional Intelligence: Educational Implications
books.author: Peter Salovey; David J. Sluyter (Eds.)
books.summary: Foundational edited volume (Basic Books) in which Mayer and Salovey present the revised four-branch ability model of emotional intelligence - the ability to monitor one's own and others' feelings, discriminate among them, and use this information to guide thinking and action - alongside chapters on emotional development and its educational implications.
key_concepts: Perceiving, using, understanding, and managing emotions
books.clinical_usage: Primary-source grounding for the ability model that underlies the MSCEIT; useful when explaining to trainees or clients what EI formally is and is not.

books.title: Emotional Intelligence: Science and Myth
books.author: Gerald Matthews; Moshe Zeidner; Richard D. Roberts
books.summary: Critical scientific appraisal (MIT Press) of the EI construct: the ability to identify, express, and understand emotions, assimilate emotions into thought, and regulate emotions. The authors examine evidence for and against EI as a distinct intelligence and scrutinize measurement, validity, and popular claims.
books.clinical_usage: Guards clinicians against over-claiming; supports evidence-based framing of EI in reports, supervision, and patient psychoeducation.

books.title: Emotional Intelligence
books.author: Daniel Goleman
books.summary: The foundational best-seller that popularized emotional intelligence, arguing that self-awareness, self-regulation, motivation, empathy, and social skill can matter more than IQ for life outcomes, drawing on affective neuroscience and psychology of the era.
books.clinical_usage: Accessible psychoeducation resource for clients; historically foundational text for understanding how EI entered clinical and public discourse.

books.title: Permission to Feel
books.author: Marc Brackett
books.summary: By the founding director of the Yale Center for Emotional Intelligence (professor, Yale Child Study Center, Yale School of Medicine). Presents the RULER framework - Recognizing, Understanding, Labeling, Expressing, and Regulating emotions - and the science of emotion skills for wellbeing at home, school, and work.
key_concepts: Emotional climate in schools and families
books.clinical_usage: Practical, evidence-informed framework clinicians can adapt for emotion-skills training with adolescents, families, and adult clients with low emotional awareness.

books.title: Emotional Intelligence in Education
books.author: Kateryna V. Keefer; James D. A. Parker; Donald H. Saklofske (Eds.)
books.summary: Academic edited volume integrating EI research with educational practice, covering EI theory and measurement in young people, social-emotional learning programs, and applications for student wellbeing and achievement.
books.clinical_usage: Supports child/adolescent clinicians collaborating with schools and designing SEL-informed interventions or recommendations.

books.title: Emotion Regulation in Psychotherapy
books.author: Robert L. Leahy; Dennis Tirch; Lisa A. Napolitano
books.summary: Practitioner guide to assessing and treating emotion regulation difficulties in psychotherapy, offering cognitive-behavioral, schema-based, mindfulness, and acceptance-based techniques for helping clients identify, tolerate, and modify emotional responses.
books.clinical_usage: Session-ready techniques for clients whose presenting problems involve poor emotion identification and regulation - the clinical core of low EI.

books.title: Handbook of Emotion Regulation (Second Edition)
books.author: James J. Gross (Ed.)
books.summary: Definitive scholarly handbook on emotion regulation science, including the process model of emotion regulation (situation selection/modification, attentional deployment, cognitive change, response modulation), neural bases, development, and psychopathology links.
books.clinical_usage: Scientific backbone for the 'managing emotions' branch of EI; informs mechanism-based treatment selection for mood, anxiety, and personality disorders.

books.title: DBT Skills Training Manual, Second Edition
books.author: Marsha M. Linehan
books.summary: The standard clinical manual for teaching dialectical behavior therapy skills, including a full emotion regulation module (identifying and labeling emotions, checking the facts, opposite action, reducing vulnerability) plus mindfulness, distress tolerance, and interpersonal effectiveness modules.
books.clinical_usage: Manualized, evidence-based curriculum for directly building the emotional skills that constitute applied EI, especially for emotion dysregulation and borderline personality disorder.

books.title: Emotion-Focused Therapy
books.author: Leslie S. Greenberg
books.summary: Overview of emotion-focused therapy (American Psychological Association) by its principal developer: theory of emotion as adaptive information, emotional awareness and expression, transforming maladaptive emotion with adaptive emotion, and the therapist's role in emotion coaching.
books.clinical_usage: Core therapeutic modality for increasing clients' emotional awareness, labeling, and processing - directly operationalizing EI constructs in psychotherapy.

papers.title: Robust associations of emotional intelligence with human flourishing: A second-order meta-analysis
papers.source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (PNAS) via PubMed (PMID 42090251; DOI 10.1073/pnas.2532963123)
papers.summary: Second-order meta-analysis synthesizing 62 meta-analyses (over 3,000 studies, roughly 1 million participants) on emotional intelligence and flourishing outcomes.
key_findings: Overall EI-flourishing correlation r = 0.28 (95% CI 0.25-0.31)
Favorable associations across cognitive ability, psychological adjustment, mental health, and work performance
Consistent across age groups and cultures; self-report EI showed larger effects than objective measures
Substantial heterogeneity; authors call for moderator research
papers.clinical_relevance: Strongest current evidence that EI is a broad, robust correlate of mental health and adjustment - supports EI assessment and skill-building as transdiagnostic clinical targets.

papers.title: Emotional intelligence predicts academic performance: A meta-analysis
papers.authors: MacCann C, Jiang Y, Brown LER, Double KS, Bucich M, Minbashian A
papers.summary: Meta-analysis of 158 citations (42,529 participants) on EI and academic performance across measurement types.
key_findings: Overall corrected correlation rho = .20; ability EI rho = .24, mixed EI rho = .19, self-rated EI rho = .12
EI added 1.7-3.9% incremental variance beyond intelligence and personality
EI was the third most important predictor after intelligence and conscientiousness
Proposed mechanisms: emotion regulation, social relationships, content overlap
papers.clinical_relevance: Quantifies EI's independent contribution to functioning in youth; supports EI-focused intervention for students presenting with academic and emotional difficulties.

papers.title: Comprehensive meta-analysis of emotional intelligence
papers.authors: Chen YC, Chiang YC, Chu HC
papers.summary: Meta-analysis of relationships between emotional intelligence and workplace variables including support, satisfaction, and stressors.
key_findings: EI correlated positively with social support, organizational factors, and satisfaction
EI correlated negatively with workplace stressors
EI framed as emotion awareness, regulation capacity, empathy, and relationship skills
Recommends organizational emotional-management training programs
papers.clinical_relevance: Relevant for occupational-health formulations and for clinicians advising on workplace stress, burnout prevention, and return-to-work planning.

papers.title: Effectiveness of emotional intelligence training on nurses' and nursing students' emotional intelligence, resilience, stress, and communication skills: a systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.authors: Kawashima T, Ota Y, Aikawa G, Watanabe M, Ashida K, Sakuramoto H
papers.source: Nurse Education Today via PubMed (PMID 40233578; DOI 10.1016/j.nedt.2025.106743)
papers.summary: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 23 randomized controlled trials of EI training for nurses and nursing students.
key_findings: EI training significantly increased emotional intelligence (SMD = 1.76)
Psychological stress decreased (SMD = -1.51)
Communication skills improved substantially (SMD = 2.72)
Resilience change was not statistically significant
papers.clinical_relevance: RCT-level evidence that EI is trainable in health professionals, with meaningful downstream effects on stress and communication - a template for clinician wellbeing programs.

papers.title: Training emotional competencies at the workplace: a systematic review and metaanalysis
papers.authors: Mehler M, Balint E, Gralla M, Poessnecker T, Gast M, Hoelzer M, Koesters M, Guendel H
papers.summary: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 50 studies (27 controlled) on workplace training of emotional intelligence, empathy, and emotion regulation.
key_findings: Moderate effects: pre-post SMD = 0.44 (95% CI 0.29-0.59); controlled SMD = 0.46 (95% CI 0.30-0.63)
Training effects persisted beyond three months
Benefits comparable across teachers, healthcare workers, and managers
High heterogeneity and low methodological quality noted; better RCTs needed
papers.clinical_relevance: Supports durable trainability of emotional competencies in adults; useful evidence base when recommending structured EI training as an adjunct to therapy.

papers.title: Emotional Intelligence and Aggressive Behaviors in Adolescents: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
papers.authors: Vega A, Cabello R, Megias-Robles A, Gomez-Leal R, Fernandez-Berrocal P
papers.source: Trauma, Violence, & Abuse via PubMed (PMID 33568015; DOI 10.1177/1524838021991296)
papers.summary: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 17 studies (Medline, PsycINFO, Scopus) on EI and adolescent aggression across ability and self-report EI models.
key_findings: Adolescents with higher EI show less aggressive behavior
Effect observed across performance-based, self-report ability, and mixed EI models
EI characterized as a protective factor against adolescent aggression
papers.clinical_relevance: Positions EI skill-building as a prevention/intervention lever in adolescent anger, conduct, and school-violence presentations.

papers.title: Promoting resilience and lower stress in nurses and improving inpatient experience through emotional intelligence training in China: A randomized controlled trial
papers.authors: Mao L, Huang L, Chen Q
papers.source: Nurse Education Today via PubMed (PMID 34543939; DOI 10.1016/j.nedt.2021.105130)
papers.summary: RCT with 103 nurses (53 intervention, 50 control) in a Chinese tertiary hospital; 12-month structured EI training program.
key_findings: Intervention group significantly improved EI, resilience, and perceived stress versus control
Patient-experience differences favored intervention wards but were not significant on all subscales
Structured, sustained (12-month) delivery model
papers.clinical_relevance: Concrete RCT model for embedding EI training in clinical workforces, with wellbeing benefits for staff and suggestive benefits for patient experience.

papers.title: The Relationship between Mindfulness and Emotional Intelligence as a Protective Factor for Healthcare Professionals: Systematic Review
papers.authors: Jimenez-Picon N, Romero-Martin M, Ponce-Blandon JA, Ramirez-Baena L, Palomo-Lara JC, Gomez-Salgado J
papers.source: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health via PubMed (PMID 34065519; DOI 10.3390/ijerph18105491)
papers.summary: Systematic review of 10 studies (2010-2020) on links between mindfulness and emotional intelligence/competencies in healthcare workers and students.
key_findings: Positive relationship between mindfulness and emotion regulation capacity
Mindfulness training associated with reduced emotional exhaustion
Benefits for emotional awareness, acceptance, and emotion recognition
Supports mindfulness-based training as a protective factor for clinician wellbeing
papers.clinical_relevance: Justifies combining mindfulness practices with EI skill-building in both clinician self-care and client interventions.

papers.title: Impact of therapist emotional intelligence on psychotherapy
papers.authors: Kaplowitz MJ, Safran JD, Muran CJ
papers.source: Journal of Nervous and Mental Disease via PubMed (PMID 21278535)
papers.summary: Foundational pilot study examining whether therapist emotional intelligence functions as an efficacious therapist variable in psychotherapy outcome.
key_findings: Higher-EI therapists achieved superior treatment outcomes
Higher therapist EI associated with notably lower client dropout
Therapist EI correlated with better patient assessment compliance
Early alliance ratings were not significantly related to therapist EI
papers.clinical_relevance: Directly relevant to a therapist-facing platform: therapist EI itself may be a trainable determinant of retention and outcome. Included as foundational despite age (pre-2016).

papers.title: The impact of enhancing students' social and emotional learning: a meta-analysis of school-based universal interventions
papers.authors: Durlak JA, Weissberg RP, Dymnicki AB, Taylor RD, Schellinger KB
papers.summary: Landmark meta-analysis of 213 universal school-based social and emotional learning (SEL) programs involving 270,034 K-12 students.
key_findings: Significant improvements in social-emotional skills, attitudes, behavior, and academic performance
11-percentile-point gain in academic achievement
Programs effectively delivered by regular school staff
Outcomes moderated by use of four recommended (SAFE) practices and implementation quality
papers.clinical_relevance: Foundational evidence (included despite age) that emotional-competence training at scale improves youth mental-health-relevant outcomes; underpins school-linked recommendations for child clients.

videos.title: Social Intelligence | Daniel Goleman | Talks at Google
videos.description: Psychologist Daniel Goleman discusses Social Intelligence: The New Science of Human Relationships, covering the social brain, empathy, and how emotional/social capacities shape relationships and performance (Authors@Google series, ~1.2M views).
videos.clinical_usage: Foundational orientation to the interpersonal dimension of EI; useful for trainee education and client psychoeducation on empathy and social connection. Older talk retained as foundational.

videos.title: Focus: the Hidden Driver of Excellence | Daniel Goleman | Talks at Google
videos.description: Goleman on attention as the underrated basis of self-awareness, self-regulation, and empathy - the attentional foundations of emotional intelligence.
videos.clinical_usage: Frames attention training (including mindfulness) as a mechanism for building EI; supports rationale-giving in attention/mindfulness-based interventions.

videos.title: Can Machines Perceive Emotion? | Dr. Lisa Feldman Barrett | Talks at Google
videos.description: Distinguished psychologist and neuroscientist Lisa Feldman Barrett explains the theory of constructed emotion and why emotion perception - by machines or people - is context-dependent rather than a simple readout of universal expressions.
videos.clinical_usage: Sharpens clinician thinking about the 'perceiving emotions' branch of EI, emotion granularity, and cultural/contextual variability in emotional expression.

videos.title: Emotional First Aid | Guy Winch | Talks at Google
videos.description: Licensed psychologist Guy Winch presents practical strategies for treating failure, rejection, guilt, and other everyday psychological injuries - applied emotional self-care and regulation skills.
videos.clinical_usage: Ready-made psychoeducational content on emotional hygiene that clinicians can assign to clients building day-to-day emotion management skills.

videos.title: Marc Brackett: Permission to Feel
videos.source: Institute of Coaching (McLean Hospital / Harvard Medical School affiliate)
videos.description: Yale Center for Emotional Intelligence founding director Marc Brackett presents the science behind Permission to Feel and the RULER framework for recognizing, understanding, labeling, expressing, and regulating emotions.
videos.clinical_usage: Structured overview of the RULER skills sequence clinicians can adapt for emotion-skills coaching with clients, families, and schools.

videos.title: Emotional Intelligence 2.0
videos.description: UCTV program (recorded 03/24/2016) in which Travis Bradberry discusses what EQ is, why unlike IQ it can be improved, and concrete strategies for developing emotional intelligence at work.
videos.clinical_usage: Accessible university-hosted introduction for clients and staff on trainable EI skills, particularly in occupational contexts.

videos.title: Richie Davidson - The Emotional Life of Your Brain (Complete)
videos.source: Dalai Lama Center for Peace and Education (public talk co-hosted with UBC Institute for Mental Health)
videos.description: Affective neuroscientist Richard Davidson (University of Wisconsin-Madison) presents the six emotional-style dimensions from The Emotional Life of Your Brain and evidence that emotional patterns are neuroplastic and trainable.
videos.clinical_usage: Neuroscience-based framework for individual differences in emotional style; supports formulation and hope-instilling psychoeducation about emotional change.

videos.title: 11. Human Behavioral Biology: Limbic System 1 by Robert Sapolsky
videos.source: Stanford School of Humanities and Sciences
videos.description: Stanford lecture by Robert Sapolsky on the limbic system - the neural circuitry of emotion - as part of the Human Behavioral Biology course.
videos.clinical_usage: Rigorous neuroscience background on the emotional brain underlying EI constructs; suited to clinician continuing education rather than client viewing.

videos.title: Psychologist Marc Brackett: Why Emotional Intelligence is Key to a Life Well Lived
videos.source: Welldoing (UK therapist-matching organization; Psychotherapy & Counselling channel)
videos.description: Interview with Yale psychologist Marc Brackett, in conversation with therapist Alice McGurran, on emotion skills, the RULER approach, and why emotional intelligence underpins wellbeing.
videos.clinical_usage: Conversational deep-dive suitable for client homework or trainee discussion on emotion labeling and regulation; channel is therapy-sector media rather than a university (see collection notes).

Channel caveats: 'Dalai Lama Center for Peace and Education' (item 7) and 'Welldoing' (item 9) are adjacent to, not squarely within, the trusted-channel categories; both feature credentialed academic psychologists/neuroscientists and were retained with this note. Items 1 and 6-7 predate 2016 but feature foundational figures (Goleman, Davidson). Papers: Kaplowitz 2011 and Durlak 2011 exceed the 10-year window and are included as foundational (therapist-EI outcome pilot; landmark SEL meta-analysis). Books: titles/authors/years verified via publisher pages (Wiley, MIT Press, Basic Books/Hachette) and Open Library; some subtitles omitted where not directly verified; publishers named in summaries only where confirmed. Research constraint: the session's WebSearch budget was exhausted before this task began, so all verification used WebFetch against PubMed/NCBI E-utilities, Open Library, publisher pages, DuckDuckGo HTML results, and YouTube oEmbed.
